Technical Specifications The following are minimum indicative specifications. The final specifications shall be confirmed by the Hos pital Administrator in consultation with a qualified engineer before publication. 4.1 Industrial Washing Machine Front-loading, hygiene-barrier or open-pocket type. Total rated washing capacity of at least 100 kg per wash cycle.

One machine of 100 kg. Stainless steel drum and body. Programmable wash cycles suitable for hospital linen. Hot-wash facility appropriate for the hospital's linen-processing requirements. Appropriate safety devices, operating controls and emergency-stop arrangements. Installation, commissioning and operator training included. 4.2 Hydro Extractor – 25 kg Rated capacity of 25 kg. Stainless steel basket. Suitable balancing and vibration-control arrangements. Safety lid interlock and braking mechanism. Safe and stable operation at the manufacturer's rated speed. 4.3 Tumble Dryers – 30 kg Each Two units, each with a rated capacity of 30 kg. Stainless steel drum. Heating system: [Steam / Electric / Gas — to be finalised before tender publication]. Temperature control and suitable drying programmes. Lint filter and automatic safety cut-off. All necessary accessories and installation included. 4.4 Laundry Trolleys – 6 Units Stainless steel construction. Smooth swivel castor wheels. Easy-to-clean surfaces and suitable load-bearing capacity for wet linen. Corrosion-resistant construction and safe handling arrangements. 4.5 Sorting Tables and Racks – 3 Sets Stainless steel construction. Smooth, easy-to-clean surfaces. Dimensions and configuration suitable for the available laundry-room space. Suitable for segregation and handling of soiled and clean linen. 4.6 Electrical and Plumbing Works – 1 Lot The contractor shall provide all electrical and plumbing works required for the safe installation and operati on of the equipment, including: Power supply connections, wiring, switches and protective devices. Proper earthing and electrical safety arrangements. Water supply and drainage connections. Steam or hot-water connections, as applicable to the approved equipment. Necessary installation accessories, fittings, testing and commissioning. Civil modifications are excluded from this contract. Any estimate or bill of quantities for the specified work shall be approved and countersigned by a qualified civil engineer or the PWD, in accordance with the appli cable provisions of the IPA Grant Manual. 5. General Quality and Performance Requirements

The supplied equipment shall: 1. Be new, unused and of a recognised make and model. 2. Carry a minimum two-year warranty from the date of acceptance. 3. Have spare parts available for at least 10 years. 4. Include installation, testing and commissioning. 5. Include training for the designated laundry staff. 6. Include user manuals, maintenance manuals and warranty documents. 7. Be supported by a valid supplier GST invoice. 8. Comply with applicable safety standards and relevant statutory requirements. The bidder shall identify the manufacturer, model number, country of origin where required, rated capacity , utility requirements and warranty conditions for every major item. 6. Eligibility and Documents to Be Submitted Bidders shall submit the following documents, as applicable under the approved procurement rules: 1. 2. 1. Earnest Deposits money Rs.15 Lakh, OEM Turnover 90 Lakhs 3. 2. Certificate of incorporation, registration or constitution of the firm. 4. 3. PAN and GST registration certificates. 5. 4. Manufacturer authorisation, where the bidder is an authorised dealer. 6. 5. Technical brochures and product datasheets. 7. 6. Evidence of experience in supplying and installing industrial laundry or comparable equipment. 8. Details of service facilities, qualified technicians and after-sales support. 9. 7. Undertaking that the equipment shall be new and unused. 10. 11. 8. Average turn of the firm is not less than 15 lacs for last three financial year. Copies of profit & loss account and balance sheets duly authenticated by a Chartered Accountant for the last two years sh ould be enclosed. 12. 9. Copy of Income Tax Return Filed Acknowledgements for last three financial years. 13. 10. Notarized Declaration-Cum-Undertaking on Non-Judicial Stamp Rs. 100/- Paper stati ng that : A. The firm has accepted all the terms and conditions as notified in the tender notice. B. There is no pending litigation, dispute, arbitration, court case, vigilance case, or any o ther proceeding against firm with any Central Government Department, State Govern ment Department, Public Sector Undertaking (PSU), Government Autonomous Body, St atutory Authority, Organization, Institution, or Agency or private individual C. All documents uploaded in the GEM Portal must be submitted in hard copy (mandatorily) also for t echnical evaluation and official verification 7. Bid Submission Procedure Bids shall be submitted online through the designated e-procurement portal within the prescribed deadline . Hardcopy of the Technical bid documents of the must be submitted in the office of the Superintendent on or before13/11/2026 up to 1:00 PM The bid shall contain two separate components: .

9. Bid Evaluation and Selection The bids shall be evaluated in the following sequence: Stage 1: Preliminary scrutiny The Procurement Committee shall check timely submission, required documents, bidder eligibility and com pliance with the published tender conditions. Stage 2: Technical evaluation The Committee shall examine whether the offered equipment meets the minimum specifications, capacity requirements, warranty, installation, training and three-year maintenance requirements. Bids that fail material technical requirements shall be treated in accordance with the tender conditions. Stage 3: Financial evaluation The financial bids of technically responsive bidders shall be evaluated on the basis of the total consolidate d price for the complete turnkey package, including GST, delivery, installation, electrical and plumbing wor k, and all three years of comprehensive maintenance. Stage 4: Recommendation and approval The technically responsive bidder quoting the lowest evaluated total price (L1) shall be recommended. . 11. Delivery, Installation and Commissioning The successful bidder shall complete delivery, installation, testing and commissioning within 30 days fro m the date of issue of the supply order, unless an amendment is approved in accordance with the ap plicable rules. The bidder shall: 1. Coordinate with the Hospital Administrator before delivery. 2. Deliver all equipment to the designated hospital premises. 3. Complete electrical and plumbing works covered by the contract. 4. Install and commission each machine safely. 5. Demonstrate the operation and performance of each item. 6. Train the designated hospital staff. 7. Hand over manuals, warranty certificates, service contacts and maintenance schedules. 8. Submit the completion report and supporting documents. The contractor shall not undertake excluded civil modifications without separate approval and the appropri ate procurement authorisation. 12. Inspection and Acceptance Following delivery and installation, the Procurement Committee, with appropriate technical assistance, sha ll inspect and test the equipment against the supply order and approved specifications. The inspection shall include: Verification of make, model, quantity and rated capacity. Physical inspection for damage and completeness. Functional testing of each machine.

Verification of electrical and plumbing safety. Confirmation of training and documentation. Verification of warranty and maintenance commitments. Any deficiency shall be recorded and rectified in accordance with the contract. Acceptance shall be documented in an inspection and acceptance report. The accepted equipment shall th en be handed over for entry in the applicable stock and asset registers and for issue to the responsible ho spital unit. 13. Warranty and Maintenance Conditions The supplier shall provide a minimum two-year warranty from the date of acceptance and comprehensive maintenance for three years in accordance with the approved contract. The maintenance contract shall specify: Quarterly preventive maintenance visits. A complaint response time of 24 hours. A repair time of 72 hours, subject to the final approved service conditions. Coverage of repair and replacement of parts. Service reports for each visit. Separate prices for each maintenance year. A clear commencement date and end date for the maintenance obligation. Maintenance payments shall be made quarterly or annually in arrears, as specified in the final tender and contract, against verified maintenance performance, the applicable invoice and certification by the authori sed officials. The tender shall clearly distinguish the warranty period from the three-year comprehensive maintenance o bligation to avoid any ambiguity in the supplier's responsibilities. 14. Submission of performance security The successful bidder shall submit a Performance Security equivalent to 5% of the total contract v alue within the prescribed period. The Performance Security shall be liable to forfeiture, in whole or in part , in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract, if the supplier fails to execute the contract or breaches its contractual obligations. 15. Payment Terms Payment for supplied equipment and completed installation works shall be processed against the original i nvoice, inspection and acceptance documentation, and other required supporting records. Payment shall be made within seven days of receipt of the complete and verified invoice, subject to the ap plicable Grant Manual provisions and completion of the required certification and approval process. Payment shall be made through electronic transfer or account-payee cheque, as permitted under the appli cable rules. Maintenance payments shall be made in arrears at the approved quarterly or annual frequency, against sa tisfactory service records and verification of performance. No payment shall be made for equipment or work that has not been supplied, completed, verified and acc epted in accordance with the contract.

18. Right to Accept or Reject Bids The procuring authority reserves the right to accept or reject bids, cancel the tender or take other permitte d action in accordance with the published tender conditions and applicable procurement rules. Any such a ction shall be recorded and approved by the competent authority. . 6. Forms of EMD and PBG Bidders can also submit the EMD with Banker’s Cheque in favour of Superintendent, AMCH, Dibrugarh payable at State Bank of India, AMC Branch . Bidder has to upload scanned copy / proof of the BC along with bid and has to ensure delivery of hardcopy to the Buyer within 5 days of Bid End date / Bid Opening date. 7. Forms of EMD and PBG Successful Bidder can submit the Performance Security in the form of Fixed Deposit Receipt also (besides PBG which is allowed as per GeM GTC). FDR should be made out or pledged in the name of Superintendent, AMCH, Dibrugarh A/C (Name of the Seller). The bank should certify on it that the deposit can be withdrawn only on the demand or with the sanction of the pledgee. For release of Security Deposit, the FDR will be released in favour of bidder by the Buyer after making endorsement on the back of the FDR duly signed and stamped along with covering letter. Successful Bidder has to upload scanned copy of the FDR document in place of PBG and has to ensure delivery of hard copy of Original FDR to the Buyer within 15 days of award of contract.
